short: Alloyed metal, writing and the first states and empires.
full:
The Bronze Age begins around 3300 BCE, when smiths learned to alloy copper with tin to make a metal far harder than either. Because tin is rare and rarely found beside copper, bronze demanded long-distance trade — and the administration to manage it.

This is the age of the first writing systems: cuneiform in Mesopotamia, hieroglyphs in Egypt, Linear B in Mycenaean Greece. Cities, palaces, codified law and standing armies appear alongside them. It closes around 1200 BCE in the eastern Mediterranean with the Late Bronze Age collapse, when a tightly interconnected world of palace economies unravelled within a couple of generations.
